demo_input.text: translate English to German: The house is beautiful.

step_explanations.title: Validate Input with Task Prefix
step_explanations.description: Check that input has a valid task prefix (translate, summarize, etc.) and text.

input_preview.text: translate English to German: The house is beautiful.

step_explanations.why_it_matters: T5 requires a task prefix to know what to do. Without it, the model doesn't know the expected output format.

step_explanations.title: Tokenize with SentencePiece & Encode
step_explanations.description: Use SentencePiece to tokenize input text and convert to token IDs for the encoder.

input_preview.text: translate English to German: The house is beautiful.

step_explanations.why_it_matters: SentencePiece is language-agnostic (no dependency on English tokenization). Works for all languages.

step_explanations.title: T5 Encoder (6 Layers)
step_explanations.description: Process input through the encoder's 6 Transformer layers to create contextualized representations of the input.
step_explanations.formula: Encoder: SelfAttention → Add&Norm → FeedForward → Add&Norm (×6 layers)
step_explanations.why_it_matters: The encoder creates a rich representation of the input that the decoder will use for generation.

step_explanations.title: T5 Decoder (Autoregressive Generation)
step_explanations.description: The decoder generates output tokens autoregressively, using cross-attention to attend to encoder outputs.
step_explanations.why_it_matters: This is where the actual translation/summarization happens. The decoder uses both its own history and the encoder's input representation.

step_explanations.title: Decode Output Tokens to Text
step_explanations.description: Convert generated token IDs back to text using SentencePiece decoder.
step_explanations.why_it_matters: Final output that users see - the result of the text-to-text transformation.

formula_cards.title: T5 Input Format (Text-to-Text)
formula_cards.explanation: Every task is cast as text-to-text. The model learns to map input text (with task prefix) to output text.
formula_cards.example: Input: 'translate English to German: The house is beautiful.' → Output: 'Das Haus ist wunderschön.'

formula_cards.title: Masked Span Corruption (Pre-training)
formula_cards.explanation: T5 masks random spans (not just single tokens) and predicts the masked spans as a sequence. This teaches the model to understand and generate text.
formula_cards.example: Original: 'The house is beautiful.' → Masked: 'The <X> is <Y>.' → Target: '<X> house <Y> beautiful'

formula_cards.title: Encoder-Decoder Attention
formula_cards.formula: DecoderAttention(Q_d, K_e, V_e) = softmax(Q_d K_e^T / √d_k) V_e
formula_cards.explanation: The decoder attends to the encoder's output (all input tokens), not just previous decoder tokens. This is cross-attention.
formula_cards.example: When generating 'wunderschön', the decoder looks at all encoder outputs for 'The house is beautiful.'

hover_annotations.definition: A text string at the start of input that tells T5 what task to perform (e.g., 'translate:', 'summarize:').
hover_annotations.formula_meaning: input = prefix + ': ' + text; model learns to condition on prefix
hover_annotations.example: 'translate English to German: Hello.' → model knows to translate to German
hover_annotations.common_mistake: Forgetting the colon after the task prefix (T5 expects 'prefix: text' format)

hover_annotations.definition: Attention mechanism in the decoder that allows it to attend to encoder outputs (the input text representation).
hover_annotations.formula_meaning: CrossAttention(Q_d, K_e, V_e) - Q comes from decoder, K/V come from encoder
hover_annotations.example: When generating 'wunderschön', decoder cross-attention focuses on 'beautiful' in the encoder output
hover_annotations.common_mistake: Thinking decoder only attends to its own previous tokens (it also attends to all encoder outputs via cross-attention)

references.title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
references.relevance: T5 paper introducing the text-to-text framework that unifies all NLP tasks.

references.title: T5: Text-To-Text Transfer Transformer (Official Blog)
references.relevance: Accessible overview of T5's text-to-text framework and pre-training objectives.

receiver_mode_explanations.explanation: T5 can do any NLP task if you tell it what to do in words. Say 'translate:' and it translates. Say 'summarize:' and it summarizes.
receiver_mode_explanations.teaching_notes: Demo translation and summarization with simple examples. Show how task prefix changes the output.

receiver_mode_explanations.explanation: T5 uses an encoder-decoder Transformer. All tasks are text-to-text: 'task: input' → 'output'. Pre-training: masked span corruption (predict masked spans).
receiver_mode_explanations.technical_detail: Encoder processes input, decoder generates output with cross-attention to encoder. Uses relative position biases instead of absolute positions.

receiver_mode_explanations.explanation: T5's text-to-text framework is elegant and unified. Research shows span corruption is more sample-efficient than token-level MLM. T5-XXL (11B) was SOTA on many benchmarks. Limitations: slower inference (encoder-decoder), larger than encoder-only models.
receiver_mode_explanations.technical_detail: Limitations: encoder-decoder is slower than encoder-only for understanding tasks. Variants: mT5 (multilingual), ByT5 (byte-level), UL2 (unified pre-training with different corruption strategies).

receiver_mode_explanations.explanation: T5-small: 60M params, 6 layers each for encoder/decoder. Use HuggingFace. For inference, it's O((n_enc² + n_dec²)×d) per generation step.
receiver_mode_explanations.technical_detail: Complexity: O(L×n²×d) for both encoder and decoder. API: transformers.T5ForConditionalGeneration, transformers.pipeline('translation', model='t5-small').

receiver_mode_explanations.explanation: T5 unifies NLP tasks under one framework. Great for teaching transfer learning and multi-task learning.
receiver_mode_explanations.teaching_notes: Quiz: Why is text-to-text elegant? Exercise: Convert classification, NER, and summarization to text-to-text format. Discuss: When would you use T5 vs. BERT vs. GPT?

research_context: T5 (Raffel et al., 2019) unified all NLP tasks into a text-to-text framework, showing that a single model can perform translation, summarization, Q&A, and classification by framing them as text input → text output. This simplified multi-task learning and transfer learning.

teaching_notes.summary: T5 casts all NLP tasks as text-to-text, using an encoder-decoder Transformer pre-trained with masked span corruption.
quiz_questions: How does T5 unify different NLP tasks into a single framework?
What is masked span corruption, and how does it differ from BERT's MLM?
When would you use T5 vs. BERT vs. GPT? Give examples.
classroom_demo_tips: Demo 3+ tasks (translation, summarization, Q&A) with the same model
common_misconceptions: T5 is just like BERT (false - it's encoder-decoder, not encoder-only)
T5 can only do one task (false - it's multi-task via text-to-text framing)
